results.title: Different types of customer feedback (and what to do with them)
results.content:
With negative ones, ask to discuss it further. You may be able to resolve whatever triggered the bad review. Brownie points if you go back and let whoever complained know when you’ve fixed the issues.

### Social media mentions

Customers don’t always come to you with feedback. Sometimes they share it where their friends and followers can see. Posts on X, LinkedIn, and Reddit all count. TikTok comments and YouTube replies do too.

A frustrated customer might post about a feature that’s broken. A delighted one might post a workflow they built with your product. Both are useful signals you’d never see in a survey.

Why this type of customer feedback matters [...] See if they’ll leave a review on G2, GetApp, or Capterra
 Ask for a testimonial for social proof
 See if they’d be willing to be featured as a case study on your website
 Ask if they know anyone who might want to use your product

Don’t be pushy about this. You don’t want to ruin the good impression they have of you by being annoying.

### Customer complaints

While it’s always nice to be praised, there’s value in negative feedback too. Praise usually comes from happy customers that aren’t having any problems. That’s great. On its own, it doesn’t give you much direction to improve.

An unhappy customer can highlight areas you can improve. Train your customer support team to dig in and uncover the actionable feedback behind complaints.

results.content:
Title: Tags are completely broken - super frustrating : r/MonarchMoney
# Tags are completely broken - super frustrating : r/MonarchMoney. Skip to main contentTags are completely broken - super frustrating : r/MonarchMoney. Image 1 Go to MonarchMoney. # Tags are completely broken - super frustrating. TL,DR: Tags disappear when you split a transaction and it’s insanely frustrating to go back, find, and retag transactions after you split them. I’m really trying hard to stick with Monarch but things like this are making it very difficult. Tags are a huge part of my workflow as I tag all my trips I take with friends and use them to track reimbursements and what people owe me. So this is an example where I’d tag all the expenses/income for a trip and then go back into the transactions of that tag and split transactions to track reimbursements. However, when I split any transaction, the tags disappear!! This causes me to have to go back, search for the transactions that I split, and then retag them. I also wish tags were just in a dropdown like categories, it’s so annoying having to open the transaction everytime to add a tag! I'm also working on the ability to split transactions via rules, and update their tags or copy over the tags from the main transaction automatically. I have a shared credit card that I split equally with a SO and the amount of time I spend splitting all of our transactions so they fit my personal budget is wild. In Mint, I could give a transaction a “reimbursed” tag and that would also automatically set it to hide from trends view. I noticed this issue about a month ago and submitted feedback through the site itself, but the immediate response on Reddit is making me wonder if those are just falling into a bottomless pit... One of the benefits of Reddit is we're able to see how many people +1 the report as an issue they also see, so we're investigating how to recreate that somewhere other than reddit. A suggestion :: It's easier and less work to track reimbursements counter-posting the reimbursements to the same category as the original expense IF the reimbursement comes in as a sync'd transaction.
